definition: Unique short identifier for the cable system within this dataset.
other-metadata: Format: short slug, lowercase, hyphenated (e.g. 'equiano', '2africa', 'seacom-1'). Primary key. Comments: assign sequentially; never reuse a retired ID.
data-collection-guidelines: Assigned by the dataset compiler. Must be unique. Keep stable across dataset versions so external references do not break.

definition: Official/common name of the submarine cable system.
other-metadata: Format: free text (proper noun). Comments: use the name used by the owner/consortium; record alternative or former names in 'notes'.
data-collection-guidelines: Source from the cable owner's official materials or the system's TeleGeography/Submarine Networks entry. Prefer the operator's own spelling and capitalisation.

definition: Current lifecycle stage of the cable system.
other-metadata: Format: controlled vocabulary {planned, approved, under-construction, ready-for-service, in-service, upgraded, retired/decommissioned, fault-suspended}. Comments: 'in-service' = carrying live traffic.
data-collection-guidelines: Determine from the most recent authoritative source. Where status is contested or transitional, record the date of the status in 'as_of_date' and explain in 'notes'.

definition: Calendar year the project received final go-ahead (financial close, consortium agreement signed, or regulatory/board approval).
other-metadata: Format: YYYY (integer). Unit: Gregorian year. Comments: if only an announcement (not approval) is known, leave blank and note in 'notes'; do not conflate announcement with approval.
data-collection-guidelines: Cite a primary source (consortium press release, regulatory filing, financial-close announcement). Distinguish 'announced' from 'approved/financial close'. If uncertain, mark blank rather than estimate.

definition: Calendar year physical cable-lay / installation work began, or is planned to begin.
other-metadata: Format: YYYY (integer). Comments: append flag in 'date_basis' field {actual, planned, estimated}. Was previously labelled 'Build Year'.
data-collection-guidelines: Use marine-survey or cable-lay commencement where reported. If planned/estimated, record 'planned' in 'date_basis' and cite the source of the projection.

definition: Calendar year the cable entered (or is planned to enter) commercial service and began carrying live traffic. Industry-standard term for 'lit year'.
other-metadata: Format: YYYY (integer). Synonyms: 'Lit Year', 'In-Service Year'. Comments: record actual vs planned in 'date_basis'.
data-collection-guidelines: RFS dates are published by operators and tracked by TeleGeography. Where actual differs from originally planned RFS, record actual and note the original in 'notes'.

definition: Calendar year the cable is expected to be retired / decommissioned, based on its design life (typically ~25 years from RFS).
other-metadata: Format: YYYY (integer). Comments: if not officially stated, derive as RFS year + design life and flag as 'estimated' in 'date_basis'. State design life in 'notes'.
data-collection-guidelines: Prefer an officially stated design life. If estimating, use RFS + 25 years (standard subsea design life) and clearly mark as estimated; never present an estimate as confirmed.

definition: The entity with effective control over the cable system (largest shareholder, consortium lead, or sole owner).
other-metadata: Format: free text (legal entity name). Comments: name the operating/controlling entity, not a brand, where they differ. For sole-owned cables this equals the owner.
data-collection-guidelines: Identify the lead/controlling party from consortium documentation or corporate filings. Where control is disputed or unclear, record the lead funder and explain in 'notes'.

definition: Country in which the controlling owner is headquartered / domiciled.
other-metadata: Format: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, ZA, FR). Comments: relevant to sovereignty/jurisdiction analysis.
data-collection-guidelines: Use the ultimate parent's headquarters jurisdiction, tracing through holding companies where possible. Record the immediate vs ultimate parent in 'notes' if they differ.

definition: Structural model of ownership.
other-metadata: Format: controlled vocabulary {sole-owned (private), consortium, joint-venture, state-owned, public-private}. Comments: 'sole-owned (private)' captures hyperscaler-owned cables (e.g. Equiano, Umoja, Waterworth).
data-collection-guidelines: Classify from ownership documentation. Where a cable is consortium-built but one party dominates, use 'consortium' and note dominance in 'notes'.

definition: List of equity holders and their percentage stakes in the cable system.
other-metadata: Format: semicolon-separated 'Entity (NN%)' pairs (e.g. 'Remgro (30%); IPS (30%); Sanlam (15%)'). Comments: if splits are undisclosed, enter 'undisclosed' and record members in 'notes'.
data-collection-guidelines: Use disclosed equity/capacity splits from filings or operator statements only. DO NOT estimate percentages. If unpublished, state 'undisclosed' explicitly — this is itself a finding.

definition: Estimated percentage of the cable owned by African-domiciled entities.
other-metadata: Format: numeric percentage (0-100) or 'undisclosed'. Comments: central to the sovereignty analysis; derive from 'shareholders' where splits are known.
data-collection-guidelines: Compute only where shareholder splits and their nationalities are documented. Where splits are undisclosed, enter 'undisclosed' — do not guess. Show working in 'notes'.

definition: Total route length of the cable system in kilometres.
other-metadata: Format: integer, kilometres. Comments: use total system length including branches where reported; note if trunk-only.
data-collection-guidelines: Use the operator's stated system length. If only mileage is given, convert (1 mi = 1.60934 km) and note. Record whether figure is trunk-only or includes branches.

definition: Primary originating endpoint of the cable system.
other-metadata: Format: 'City, ISO country code' (e.g. 'Melkbosstrand, ZA'). Comments: 'From' and 'To' are nominal endpoints; full set of landings is in 'landings'.
data-collection-guidelines: Use the operator's designated terminal stations. For ring/looped systems, pick a conventional endpoint and explain topology in 'notes'.

definition: Primary terminating endpoint of the cable system.
other-metadata: Format: 'City, ISO country code'. Comments: see 'origin'.
data-collection-guidelines: As for 'origin'. For systems with multiple terminations, record the principal one and list the rest under 'landings'.

definition: All cable landing stations / countries where the cable comes ashore.
other-metadata: Format: semicolon-separated 'City, ISO country code' list. Comments: 'CLS' = Cable Landing Station. Order along the route where possible.
data-collection-guidelines: Compile the full landing list from operator route maps or Submarine Networks. Include planned landings for not-yet-RFS cables and flag as planned in 'notes'.

definition: Primary world region(s) the cable connects, relevant to this dataset's scope.
other-metadata: Format: controlled vocabulary, multi-value semicolon-separated {West Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa, North Africa, Europe, Middle East, South Asia, East Asia, Americas}.
data-collection-guidelines: Classify from the landing list. Keep consistent region labels across rows to allow filtering.

definition: Transmission technology generation of the cable.
other-metadata: Format: controlled vocabulary {analogue-coaxial, fibre-optic, fibre-optic-SDM}. Comments: SDM = space-division multiplexing (the high-fibre-count generation, e.g. Equiano, 2Africa).
data-collection-guidelines: Determine from system supplier specifications. Coaxial applies only to legacy/historical cables.

definition: Maximum total design capacity of the cable system in terabits per second.
other-metadata: Format: numeric, Tbps. Comments: state whether trunk-only or full system in 'notes'. For pre-fibre cables capacity may be in Gbit/s or voice circuits — record in original unit in 'notes'.
data-collection-guidelines: Use the operator's stated design capacity. Distinguish DESIGN capacity (maximum potential) from LIT/used capacity. Cite the source; note the measurement basis.

definition: Number of fibre pairs in the cable.
other-metadata: Format: integer. Comments: a 'pair' = one transmit + one receive fibre. Record working vs total if they differ. For historical cables, may be 'n/a (coaxial)'.
data-collection-guidelines: Source from system supplier / operator specs. For not-yet-built cables, use the announced pair count and flag as planned.

definition: Estimated capacity currently activated (lit) and in use, as opposed to total design capacity.
other-metadata: Format: numeric Tbps or percentage of design, with basis stated. Comments: usually far below design capacity; often estimated.
data-collection-guidelines: Lit capacity is rarely officially published; where estimated, state the basis and source and flag as 'estimated'. If unknown, leave blank — do not infer from design capacity.

definition: Parties holding capacity on the cable via Indefeasible Rights of Use (IRU) or other leases, distinct from the equity owners.
other-metadata: Format: semicolon-separated 'Entity (capacity / pairs, term)' where known (e.g. 'SEACOM (1 fibre pair, 12 Tbps IRU on Equiano)'). Comments: IRU = long-term capacity lease.
data-collection-guidelines: Record only documented IRU/lease arrangements from operator announcements. Distinguish tenants (capacity rights) from owners (equity). Cite each.

definition: Whether capacity is sold to all comers on equal, non-discriminatory terms.
other-metadata: Format: boolean {yes, no, partial, unknown}. Comments: 'open access' is a commercial-access claim, NOT a measure of ownership — keep distinct from ownership fields.
data-collection-guidelines: Use the operator's stated access model, but treat marketing claims critically. Note in 'notes' that open access does not imply local/African ownership.

definition: Total reported capital cost to build the cable system, in millions of US dollars.
other-metadata: Format: numeric, USD millions. Comments: state nominal year of figure in 'notes'; do not inflation-adjust without flagging.
data-collection-guidelines: Use reported/announced build cost from a primary source. Note the year and whether figure is total system or a segment. Mark estimates clearly.

definition: The marine systems vendor that manufactured and/or installed the cable.
other-metadata: Format: free text (e.g. 'Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN)', 'NEC', 'SubCom'). Comments: relevant to supply-chain and sovereignty analysis.
data-collection-guidelines: Source from the supply contract announcement. Where multiple suppliers built different segments, list all and note segments in 'notes'.

definition: The authoritative source(s) for this row's values.
other-metadata: Format: source name(s), semicolon-separated (e.g. 'TeleGeography; operator press release'). Comments: every row must be traceable.
data-collection-guidelines: Prefer primary sources (operator, regulator, consortium, system supplier) over aggregators. Record one source per contested field in 'notes' if sources disagree.

definition: Direct hyperlink(s) to the source evidence.
other-metadata: Format: URL(s), semicolon-separated. Comments: use stable/canonical links; archive (e.g. Wayback) where the source may change.
data-collection-guidelines: Provide a working link for verification. For paywalled/proprietary data (e.g. TeleGeography), cite the source name even if the URL is gated.

definition: Compiler's assessment of how well-evidenced the row's key figures are.
other-metadata: Format: controlled vocabulary {confirmed, reported, estimated, disputed}. Comments: supports the dataset's reliability standard.
data-collection-guidelines: 'confirmed' = primary source; 'reported' = secondary/credible media; 'estimated' = derived/inferred; 'disputed' = sources conflict. Be conservative.

definition: The date to which the row's status and capacity figures apply.
other-metadata: Format: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). Comments: capacity and status change over time; this anchors the snapshot.
data-collection-guidelines: Set to the date the figures were verified. Update when any value changes.

definition: Date this row was last edited or verified by the compiler.
other-metadata: Format: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). Comments: dataset-management field.
data-collection-guidelines: Update on every edit. Distinct from 'as_of_date', which refers to the real-world validity of the data.

definition: Free-text field for caveats, conflicting sources, methodology, synonyms, and anything not captured elsewhere.
other-metadata: Format: free text. Comments: the place to show working, especially for estimated or disputed values.
data-collection-guidelines: Use generously. Any estimate, derivation, or source conflict MUST be explained here so the figure is fully auditable.
